states.name: New York
states.grandfather: Worked as a central service technician in a health care facility for a cumulative year within the four years before January 1, 2015
states.credentials: CRCST or CSPDT, or a substantially equivalent credential from a nationally accredited central service credentialing organization
states.ceWho: Every technician who qualifies by credential or by past employment
states.facilities: General hospitals, and diagnostic and treatment centers authorized to provide ambulatory surgery
states.extra: A facility that cannot find enough qualified technicians after a documented diligent effort may hire someone who does not qualify yet; that person must hold the credential within two years of starting. Endoscope reprocessing by high-level disinfection is outside the law, per the Department of Health letter.
states.authority: New York State Department of Health

states.name: New Jersey
states.enacted: Hospital licensing standards of the New Jersey Department of Health, amended by 50 N.J.R. 552(b)
states.effectiveNote: date of the last amendment of the rule; the certification duty predates it
states.credentials: Certification through a national sterile processing program recognized by the Department of Health
states.ceWho: The rule sets no hours; the certifying body's renewal rules apply
states.extra: The director or supervisor of central service must be full time, have two years of supervisory experience and be certified. Staff who use ethylene oxide need the appropriate license from the Department of Environmental Protection.

states.name: Connecticut
states.enacted: Public Act 15-11, amended by Public Act 22-58
states.grandfather: Employed or contracted as a central service technician by a health care facility before January 1, 2016
states.facilities: Hospitals (chronic disease hospitals excluded) and outpatient surgical facilities
states.extra: Staff outside the central service department may decontaminate or sterilize equipment if the facility's infection prevention committee has trained them and found them competent; the facility keeps a list of them, and they also complete 10 hours of continuing education a year.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.enacted: Act of October 29, 2020, P.L. 710, No. 80 (House Bill 81)
states.grandfather: Employed or contracted as a central service technician by a health care facility on or before December 28, 2020, the day the act took effect
states.ceWho: Every technician the law covers, whether by certificate or by earlier work
states.facilities: Hospitals, ambulatory surgical facilities and freestanding surgical outpatient facilities
states.extra: Health care practitioners, dental assistants and people licensed under the Dental Law, supervised students and interns, and people holding a credential from a nationally accredited body to perform health services may do the work without the certification. The act states it does not apply to facilities owned or operated by the federal government.

states.name: Tennessee
states.grandfather: Employed or contracted as a central service technician in a healthcare institution before January 1, 2017
states.ceWho: Every technician the law covers, whether by certificate or by earlier work
states.facilities: Hospitals and ambulatory surgical treatment centers
states.extra: Surgical technologists, diagnostic medical sonographers and licensed providers working within their scope are not covered. Staff outside the central service department may be trained and found competent by the infection prevention committee; the institution keeps a list and they complete 10 hours of continuing education a year.

states.name: Delaware
states.enacted: 83 Del. Laws c. 493 (House Bill 279), approved October 21, 2022
states.grandfather: Employed or otherwise working as a central service technician in a health care facility as of January 1, 2023
states.ceWho: Every central service technician employed in a health care facility
states.facilities: Hospitals and freestanding surgical centers licensed under Title 16
states.extra: Health care practitioners licensed under Title 24 and supervised students or interns may do the tasks. The facility keeps proof of each technician's certification and date of hire.
states.authority: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services

states.name: Minnesota
states.enacted: Laws 2025, First Special Session, chapter 3, article 2, section 33, signed June 14, 2025
states.grandfather: Employed or retained as a central service technician by a health care facility on or before December 31, 2027
states.credentials: CRCST, CER, CSPDT or CFER (certified endoscope reprocessor or certified flexible endoscope reprocessor)
states.ceWho: Every technician the law covers, whether by certificate or by earlier work
states.extra: Because everyone employed on or before December 31, 2027 qualifies by that employment, the certification duty only bites on people hired from January 1, 2028. Health care practitioners, people credentialed by a nationally accredited body to perform health care services, and supervised students or interns are not covered.

crcst.owner: Healthcare Sterile Processing Association (HSPA, formerly IAHCSMM)
crcst.editionLabel: CRCST content outline, 2023 job task analysis
crcst.scoring: One point per correct scored answer; the passing point is set with the Angoff procedure supplemented by the Beuk compromise method and approved by the HSPA Certification Council.
crcst.passText: HSPA reports pass or fail on screen at the end of the exam; it does not publish the passing point as a number of right answers.

6 months of full-time employment in a related allied health profession and 6 months performing sterile processing activities, signed by your manager
A sterile processing technician training course passed with a grade of 70 or higher
12 months of healthcare product sales or service related to sterile processing, signed by your employer
